security_spec.violation_condition: Linux kernel context-switch, KVM world-switch, or signal-delivery code saves PCC (containing the P-bit) and later restores it without preserving the P-bit value, or writes to extended YLEN CSRs (sscratch_y, mscratch_y, vsscratch_y, stvec_y, mtvec_y, vstvec_y, sepc_y, mepc_y, vsepc_y) using CSRRW while in Address Mode without applying SCADDR semantics, causing capability metadata (tag, bounds, permissions) to be silently stripped or corrupted across privilege boundaries.
security_spec.summary: P-bit (formerly M-bit) in PCC controls CHERI Execution Mode across context switches; kernel must propagate it faithfully and respect that CSRRW writes to extended CSRs in Address Mode apply SCADDR (stripping capability metadata), otherwise a process could escape its capability bounds after resume or return-to-userspace.

findings.finding: KVM world-switch uses CSRRW on SSCRATCH (lines 57, 104, 146) and CSRRW on SSTATUS (lines 48, 155) to atomically swap host/guest context. Under Zysentry, these would become extended YLEN CSRs (sscratch_y), and CSRRW would silently strip capability metadata (tag, bounds, permissions) without SCADDR semantics. SPEC VIOLATION IF ZYSENTRY ENABLED: capability state corrupted across guest<->host transitions, enabling privilege escape via forged capabilities in the host.
findings.snippet:
csrrw	t0, CSR_SSTATUS, t0       // line 48: atomically swaps sstatus
csrrw	t1, CSR_STVEC, t1          // line 51: atomically swaps stvec
csrrw	t3, CSR_SSCRATCH, a0       // line 57: atomically swaps sscratch
csrrw	a0, CSR_SSCRATCH, a0       // line 104: guest GPR save path uses CSRRW on SSCRATCH
csrrw	t1, CSR_SSCRATCH, t1       // line 146: host restore path uses CSRRW on SSCRATCH

findings.finding: Exception entry uses CSRRW on CSR_SCRATCH (lines 131, 324, 330) for user/kernel TP swapping and csrw CSR_SCRATCH (lines 200, 273) to zero/reload scratch. Under Zysentry, CSR_SCRATCH maps to sscratch_y, and writes via CSRRW/CSRW without SCADDR semantics would strip capability tags. This is the primary exception path hit on every trap/interrupt; corruption here would affect all subsequent context-switch and signal-delivery decisions.
findings.snippet:
csrrw tp, CSR_SCRATCH, tp       // line 131: user<->kernel TP swap via SSCRATCH
csrw CSR_SCRATCH, x0            // line 200: zero scratch in kernel
csrw CSR_SCRATCH, tp            // line 273: restore scratch for user return

findings.finding: Context switch saves/restores callee-saved GPRs (ra, sp, s0-s11) and SR_SUM status bit via thread_struct. No CHERI extended state is handled because this kernel version has no CHERI support. Status register save/restore uses CSRR/CSRS on CSR_STATUS which is XLEN-width only in this codebase. No PCC, P-bit, or capability metadata exists to be corrupted.
findings.snippet:
REG_S ra,  TASK_THREAD_RA_RA(a3)     // line 426: save callee GPRs only
csrr  s0, CSR_STATUS                   // line 442: read status (XLEN only)
REG_L ra,  TASK_THREAD_RA_RA(a4)     // line 452: restore callee GPRs only
csrs  CSR_STATUS, s0                   // line 451: set SR_SUM (XLEN only)

findings.finding: VCPU load writes guest VS CSRs (VSSTATUS, VSIE, VSTVEC, VSSCRATCH, VSEPC, VSCAUSE, VSTVAL, HEDELEG, HVIP, VSATP) using csr_write/nacl_csr_write (lines 586-622). Under Zysentry, these would be extended YLEN CSRs (vsscratch_y, vstvec_y, vsepc_y), and direct writes would corrupt capability metadata. No save/restore of any CHERI-specific state exists because the feature is absent.
findings.snippet:
csr_write(CSR_VSSTATUS, csr->vsstatus);     // line 605: writes to VS SSTATUS
csr_write(CSR_VSTVEC, csr->vstvec);          // line 607: writes to VS STVEC
csr_write(CSR_VSSCRATCH, csr->vsscratch);    // line 608: writes to VS SSCRATCH
csr_write(CSR_VSEPC, csr->vsepc);            // line 609: writes to VS SEPC

findings.finding: VCPU put reads back guest VS CSRs using csr_read/nacl_csr_read (lines 663-681). Under Zysentry, reading extended YLEN CSRs back into XLEN-width storage fields in kvm_vcpu_csr (defined with 'unsigned long' at kvm_host.h:157-168) would silently truncate the upper bits containing capability metadata (P-bit, tag, bounds). The storage structure has no fields for capability state.
findings.snippet:
csr->vsscratch = csr_read(CSR_VSSCRATCH);   // line 676: reads back VS SSCRATCH
csr->vsepc = csr_read(CSR_VSEPC);            // line 677: reads back VS SEPC
csr->vstvec = csr_read(CSR_VSTVEC);          // line 675: reads back VS STVEC

findings.finding: Signal frame setup copies pt_regs (GPRs) and FP state, plus V/ZICFISS extension headers. No CHERI extension state exists to save or restore. The signal frame extension mechanism (arch_ext_list, RISCV_V_MAGIC, RISCV_ZICFISS_MAGIC) provides the correct pattern for future CHERI state, but no CHERI magic/header is defined or handled.
findings.snippet:
err = __copy_to_user(&sc->sc_regs, regs, sizeof(sc->sc_regs));  // line 362: GPRs only
ext_size = arch_ext->save(regs, sc_ext_ptr + 1);                // line 372: extension save hook

findings.finding: Signal frame restore copies back pt_regs (GPRs) and handles only RISCV_V_MAGIC and RISCV_ZICFISS_MAGIC extension headers. No CHERI capability state to restore. The extension dispatch mechanism would need a new CHERI magic to handle capability register restoration, but such code does not exist.
findings.snippet:
err = __copy_from_user(regs, &sc->sc_regs, sizeof(sc->sc_regs));  // line 226: GPRs only
case RISCV_V_MAGIC:                                                 // line 260: V ext only
case RISCV_ZICFISS_MAGIC:                                           // line 267: CFI only

findings.finding: start_thread initializes new process registers (status, epc, sp) and clears shadow stack / IBT state. No PCC or CHERI capability initialization. Under Zysentry, new processes would need their PCC initialized with appropriate bounds/permissions; this path currently has no such logic.
findings.snippet:
regs->status = SR_PIE;           // line 147: set status bits only
regs->epc = pc;                  // line 156: set entry point (not PCC)
regs->sp = sp;                   // line 157: set stack pointer (not capability)

findings.finding: Macro atomically saves host SSCRATCH and loads guest VCPU arch pointer into SSCRATCH using csrrw (line 57). Under Zysentry, sscratch_y holds a full capability; CSRRW strips tags. The guest SEPC is loaded with csrw (line 54) rather than a capability-aware instruction. Host STVEC is swapped with csrrw (line 51), which would also strip capability metadata from stvec_y.
findings.snippet:
csrrw	t1, CSR_STVEC, t1          // line 51: swap stvec (would strip stvec_y cap)
csrw	CSR_SEPC, t2               // line 54: write sepc (would strip sepc_y cap)
csrrw	t3, CSR_SSCRATCH, a0       // line 57: swap sscratch (would strip sscratch_y cap)
